drawn_text: Anthropic and Nvidia: An earlier public clash over chip-export controls, as CNBC reported it on May 1, 2025. Anthropic had argued in a post of the day before for tighter controls and enforcement ("Maintaining America's compute advantage through export controls is essential for national security and economic prosperity"), saying smugglers had hidden chips in "prosthetic baby bumps" and "packed alongside live lobsters". A Nvidia spokesperson answered: "American firms should focus on innovation and rise to the challenge, rather than tell tall tales that large, heavy, and sensitive electronics are somehow smuggled in" such ways, and: "America cannot manipulate regulators to capture victory in AI"; The Register's update of May 1 gives the first sentence of that reply, which it says Nvidia sent in response to Anthropic's note: "China, with half of the world's AI researchers, has highly capable AI experts at every layer of the AI stack". An Anthropic spokesperson told Fortune: "National security is bigger than the interest of any single company", and that it "stands by its recently filed public submission in support of strong and balanced export controls". That submission, of Apr 29, 2025, says "Anthropic strongly supports" the rule and recommends "export restrictions on certain model weights"; it asks to consider "reducing the number of H100s that Tier 2 countries can purchase without review", and the post of the next day adds two things: "Increase funding for export enforcement", and, for some countries, more chips: "We suggest allowing countries in Tier 2 with robust data center security to obtain more chips", through agreements between governments; its own words are "packing GPUs alongside live lobsters", and its footnote for the baby bumps cites a press report of 2022 about "over 200 Intel Alder Lake CPUs". Anthropic's own pages give its positions through that year: on Mar 6 it advocated "tightening semiconductor export restrictions", "controlling H20 chips" among them; on Jul 23 it wrote that "we are concerned with the Administration's recent reversal on export of the Nvidia H20 chips to China" and urged the administration "to maintain controls on the H20 chip"; on Oct 21 its chief executive wrote that the real risk is "filling the PRC's data centers with US chips they can't make themselves". On Nov 13, 2025 Reuters, relaying the Wall Street Journal, reported that the GAIN AI Act, legislation "to further curb chipmaker Nvidia's ability to export chips to China", "is also backed by AI startup Anthropic", the wire having opened that Amazon "is joining Microsoft in backing legislation" to that end and said that "Microsoft publicly came out in favor of the legislation, while officials at Amazon's cloud unit have privately told Senate staffers that they also support it"; Reuters "could not immediately verify the report", Anthropic did not immediately respond to it, and Nvidia had said the bill "stands to restrict global competition for advanced chips".
